Hospital course:
Hospital Course Summary:

This 47-year-old male patient was admitted to our institution with a diagnosis of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with multiple mutations, including DNMT3A, RUNX1, and U2AF1, along with FLT3–ITD mutation. The patient had received various treatments for his condition but did not respond well to them. After a bone marrow analysis, emergent BCR–ABL1 rearrangement was detected along with increased allelic ratio of FLT3-ITD mutation. The patient was then treated with different therapies, including CPX-351 plus venetoclax, ponatinib, and gilteritinib combination, which resulted in a marrow remission. The patient underwent allogeneic stem-cell transplantation (ASCT) and achieved full remission on day 30 post-ASCT. Unfortunately, the patient expired 8 months after ASCT due to infectious complications.

Summary of Hospital Stay:
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Treatment: CPX-351, decitabine, FLAG-IDA, single-agent gilteritinib, cladribine, idarubicin, cytarabine, sorafenib, decitabine, venetoclax, ponatinib, CPX-351 plus venetoclax, ponatinib, and gilteritinib combination, Allogeneic stem-cell transplantation
Complications: infectious complications
Outcome: Achieved Marrow remission; Achieved full remission post-ASCT

Assessment and Plan:

The patient presented with AML with FLT3–ITD, DNMT3A, RUNX1, and U2AF1 mutations that were resistant to several chemotherapy treatments. After various therapies, the patient achieved a marrow remission with the CPX-351 plus venetoclax, ponatinib, and gilteritinib combination. Allogeneic stem-cell transplantation was performed, which resulted in full remission post-ASCT. Despite successful remission, the patient died eight months post-ASCT due to infectious complications.
